NOTE: As was noted previously in 4-105, business license fees established by municipalities are imposed as an incident of the municipal police power to protect the health, safety, morals and general welfare of the pupolace. Such fees are not in and of themselves revenue-

- yaising devices, but rather are regulatory schemes to allow for the control of businesses and occupations which have potentially harmful or detrimental effects on the general public. Regulation of "harmless" or "useful" businesses is generally proscribed by the courts, and-the regulation of businesses .licensed by the State is usually prohibited.

Thus, before a municipality can impose any business license fee, it must first decide if a particular business or occupation is an appropriate candidate for regulation under the municipal police power. If it decides that it is, it may then proceed to set the amount of the fee for the particular business or occupation. Even here, however, caution is necessary, because the imposition of a business license fee exceeding to any. significant degree the actual cost of regulation can be construed as an invalid attempt to impose a tax under the guise of the police power. And a regulatory license fee simply may not be imposed for such revenue purposes...

The reader is urged to consult a recent Institute of Government publication entitled Handbook on Municipal Taxation and Licensing, University of Georgia, 1975, for an in depth analysis of this entire subject, with supporting legal citations.
